headline: All majors below the 200-day, momentum split and weakening, but whales buying spot while leverage stays crowded and funded long.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, with none of them crossed above that line and zero golden crosses in the set. That is a downtrend floor, fully intact. Against that backdrop, the momentum picture is fractured. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 47.4 and its MACD is below signal, meaning price momentum is not accelerating into that weakness; Ethereum shows 56.3 on RSI with MACD also below signal, a sign the asset is not yet oversold despite a 24-hour loss of 0.78 percent. Solana is weaker still at RSI 42.7, and XRP at 42.9, both deep in the bottom half of the oscillator range. The outliers are BNB and Doge, the only two with MACD above signal; BNB's RSI of 48.3 is still centered, and Doge's is 40.7, so even the positive MACD cross is not accompanied by a surge in the oscillator. The message is consistent: the downtrend is confirmed by structure, but momentum has not accelerated into it. Nothing is breaking lower on force; instead, the market is resting somewhere between resignation and exhaustion.

Leverage positioning reveals the crowding. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding rate is 0.0012 percent, annualizing to 1.3 percent, a modest carry but not yet inverted. More telling is the long-to-short ratio at 1.93, meaning nearly two dollars of long contracts for every dollar of shorts. That skew persists across the board: Ethereum at 2.0, Solana at 2.61, XRP at 2.98, and Doge at a stretched 4.62. In absolute terms, Bitcoin's open interest of 2.03 billion USD and Ethereum's 1.36 billion USD represent real money betting on upside in a market still positioned below its trend lines. Liquidations over the past 24 hours have been heavier on the short side across the board: Bitcoin saw 7.3 million USD of shorts liquidated versus 3.9 million of longs, and Ethereum 6.1 million of shorts versus 9.6 million of longs. The leverage book is bullishly tilted, funded to stay that way, and under pressure when price moves are not obliging. That tension, between crowded upside positioning and a downtrend structure, is the friction point.

The spot ETF window is telling a different story from the leveraged market. On July 31st, Bitcoin ETF flows printed minus 265.4 million USD in a single session, but over the prior five sessions the net was only minus 61.5 million USD, a print that understates the single-day rout. Ethereum, by contrast, has seen plus 9.0 million USD on the latest day and plus 10.0 million USD over five sessions, with positive direction holding for two consecutive days. Neither asset is seeing sustained outflow; Bitcoin's one-day bleed does not yet speak to a regime break in spot demand. The larger frame comes from whale behavior in the derivatives ecosystem: over the past 24 hours, 103.1 million USD of Bitcoin moved off exchanges, sourced entirely from Coinbase Institutional (51.5 million USD) and private outflows. That is classic accumulation behavior, a movement toward custody and away from trading venues. Stablecoin float stands at 305.4 billion USD, down 1.04 percent over 30 days, suggesting a slow drain of dry powder, but the weekly whale flow data shows violent swings (1.09 billion USD net off exchanges last period, 493 million the period before, minus 17.9 million the period before that), a sign of chop rather than a sustained unwind.

Sentiment is Fear at a reading of 28, anchored in the lower half of the 30-day range of 20 to 33. The crowd is not panicked (which would be below 20) but is decidedly pessimistic. Yet the tape does not match that weight. Fear & Greed measures collective anxiety; spot ETF outflows are measured in hundreds of millions, and whale flows are actually showing net removal of coins from exchanges, a position-taking move, not a capitulation exit. This is a meaningful divergence: the headline sentiment is down, but the marginal dollar at the whale level is buying spot and moving it to cold storage. Bitcoin dominance is 56.4 percent, stable and in the mid-range, and total market cap is up 0.66 percent on the day despite Bitcoin's 24-hour loss of 0.34 percent, a sign of relative outperformance in the altcoin sleeve.

Distance from the 12-month high is severe across the board. Bitcoin is 49 percent below its 124,773 USD high, Ethereum 60.6 percent below 4,829 USD, Solana 70.4 percent below 247.56 USD, and Cardano a striking 83.2 percent below 0.9631 USD. These are drawdowns that have culled speculative positioning and should, by historical measure, have flushed weak hands. Realized volatility at 31.5 percent for Bitcoin and up to 73 percent for Cardano speaks to churn and disagreement on value, not to climactic selling on a single day. The 90-day range for Bitcoin runs from 58,550 USD to 82,145 USD, a 40 percent span, suggesting the market has already lived through wide swings; today's price of 63,653 is in the lower half but not at the bottom.

Watch for three conditions: first, a flip in the BTC funding rate from positive to negative, which would signal shorts are now being rewarded and longs must pay to hold; that would be a structural shift in the leverage game. Second, whether the seven-day price changes turn uniformly positive across the major-seven, because a multi-day rally that reclaims assets above their 200-day averages would break the regime. Third, monitor the 24-hour whale flows over the next week; the move off exchanges today totaled 103 million USD net, a meaningful print, but it is one day and must be placed against the violent weekly swings. If coins continue flowing to cold storage or staking and spot ETF redemptions stabilize, the tape would be saying that weakness is being accumulated, not abandoned. That is what to watch.
